name: health
title: First aid
tagline: What to do in the first five minutes
notice: First-aid guidance only. It is not a diagnosis. In Canada and the US, call 911 in an emergency.

bleeding.title: Heavy bleeding
steps: Press hard on the wound with a clean cloth or your hand.
Keep pressing without lifting to look. Add more cloth on top if it soaks through.
If it is an arm or leg and you can, raise it above the heart.
Keep pressure on until help arrives.
bleeding.urgent: Call 911 if blood is spurting, will not stop after 10 minutes of pressure, or the person is pale and faint.

choking.title: Choking adult
steps: Ask: are you choking? If they can cough or speak, tell them to keep coughing.
If they cannot breathe or speak, give 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades.
Then give 5 abdominal thrusts: fist above the navel, pull sharply in and up.
Repeat 5 back blows and 5 thrusts until the object comes out.
choking.urgent: Call 911 if the object does not come out. If they go unresponsive, start CPR.

burn.title: Burn
steps: Cool the burn under cool running water for 20 minutes.
Take off rings, watches and loose clothing near the burn before it swells.
Cover loosely with cling film or a clean non-fluffy dressing.
Do not use ice, butter or creams, and do not pop blisters.
burn.urgent: Call 911 for burns larger than the person's hand, on the face, hands or groin, or caused by chemicals or electricity.

stroke.title: Possible stroke
steps: Face: ask them to smile. Does one side droop?
Arms: ask them to raise both arms. Does one drift down?
Speech: ask them to repeat a simple sentence. Is it slurred or strange?
Time: if any sign is present, call 911 now and note the time it started.
Keep them still and do not give food, drink or medicine.
stroke.urgent: Call 911 immediately for any one of these signs, even if it goes away.

cpr.title: Unresponsive and not breathing
steps: Tap their shoulders and shout. If no response, call 911 and send someone for an AED.
Lay them on their back on a firm surface.
Push hard and fast in the centre of the chest: 5 cm deep, 100 to 120 pushes per minute.
Do not stop until help or an AED arrives. Follow the AED's spoken instructions.
cpr.urgent: Call 911 first. Chest compressions alone are enough if you are untrained.

lowsugar.title: Low blood sugar
steps: If they are awake and can swallow, give 15 g of fast sugar: half a cup of juice or regular pop, or 3 to 4 glucose tablets.
Have them sit and rest for 15 minutes.
If they still feel shaky, give the same amount again.
Once better, give a snack with starch and protein.
lowsugar.urgent: Call 911 if they are drowsy, cannot swallow, or pass out. Do not put food or drink in their mouth.

allergy.title: Severe allergic reaction
steps: Ask if they carry an epinephrine auto-injector (EpiPen).
Help them use it: press it into the outer thigh and hold for several seconds.
Call 911 and say anaphylaxis.
Lay them down with legs raised, or let them sit up if breathing is hard.
A second dose can be given after 5 minutes if there is no improvement.
allergy.urgent: Call 911 even if they feel better after the injection.

heat.title: Heat exhaustion
steps: Move them to shade or a cool room.
Lay them down and raise their feet slightly.
Give cool water or a sports drink in small sips.
Cool the skin with wet cloths and fanning.
heat.urgent: Call 911 if they are confused, stop sweating with hot skin, or are not better in 30 minutes.

nosebleed.title: Nosebleed
steps: Sit them down leaning slightly forward, not back.
Pinch the soft part of the nose firmly for 10 minutes without letting go.
Have them breathe through the mouth and spit out any blood.
After it stops, no nose blowing for a few hours.
nosebleed.urgent: Get medical help if it lasts more than 20 minutes or follows a blow to the head.

seizure.title: Seizure
steps: Move hard or sharp objects away. Do not hold them down.
Cushion their head with something soft.
Do not put anything in their mouth.
Time the seizure.
When the shaking stops, roll them onto their side and stay with them.
seizure.urgent: Call 911 if it lasts more than 5 minutes, repeats, or it is their first seizure.

examples: he cut his hand and it is bleeding a lot
I burned my hand on the stove
one side of his face is drooping
